title: Advanced Custom Hooks: Composition, Lifecycle & Event-Driven Patterns
description: Design robust, type-safe custom React hooks: state composition, event-driven subscriptions, useSyncExternalStore for non-React stores, debouncing/throttling, and lifecycle resilience.

data.text: Custom hooks are React's primary mechanism for abstracting stateful behavior away from visual presentation. By decoupling business logic, network subscriptions, and state machines into headless hooks, components become purely declarative renderers. When building enterprise AI frontends, custom hooks prevent UI components from drowning in AbortController cleanup logic, SSE buffer parsing, and complex asynchronous state machines.

data.text: Pattern 1: High-Performance Debouncing with Generic Types
When users type into AI search boxes, sending vector embeddings on every keystroke exhausts API rate limits. A type-safe `useDebounce` hook guarantees that values only propagate after typing pauses.

data.title: Generic useDebounce Hook in TypeScript
data.content: Fully type-safe generic hook with automated timer cleanup on unmount.

data.text: Pattern 2: useSyncExternalStore for Tearing-Free External Subscriptions

Subscribing to browser APIs (like `navigator.onLine` or window resize) inside `useEffect` can lead to 'tearing' in React concurrent mode, where different parts of the screen render inconsistent values during the same frame. `useSyncExternalStore` guarantees synchronous, atomic reads from any external mutable store.

data.title: Network Connectivity Hook with useSyncExternalStore
data.content: Subscribing to online/offline network events with zero tearing and SSR safety.

data.text: Pattern 3: State Machine Hook with useReducer

For complex workflows—such as agent tool execution with human approvals—multiple `useState` variables lead to impossible states (e.g., `isLoading = false` while `isPendingApproval = true`). A discriminated union action reducer eliminates invalid state combinations.

data.title: Agent Execution State Machine Hook
data.content: Encapsulating tool invocation state, approvals, and error handling in a disciplined reducer.

data.text: Unit Testing Custom Hooks with renderHook
Because custom hooks cannot be invoked outside of React component rendering, use `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook` utility to assert on hook outputs and state transitions.

data.title: Testing useDebounce with Vitest / Jest
data.content: Using fake timers and act() to verify that the debounced value only updates after the delay threshold.

data.title: Custom Hook Engineering Standards
items: Always prefix hook function name with 'use' (enforces ESLint react-hooks rules)
Return object or tuple with consistent naming (prefer objects for >2 return values)
Never violate the Rules of Hooks: no conditional hooks, no loops, call only at top level
Use useSyncExternalStore when reading from external browser APIs or non-React state stores
Clean up all event listeners, intervals, and network abort controllers in effect cleanup functions
Verify hook behavior with isolated renderHook unit tests covering edge cases

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: Custom hooks decouple complex stateful logic from presentation components.
Generic typing allows hooks like useDebounce to operate safely across arbitrary data types.
useSyncExternalStore prevents concurrent rendering tearing when reading external state.
Next, we explore performance optimization techniques: memoization, virtualization, and bundle tuning.
data.takeaway: Great React code is composed of headless, type-safe custom hooks that encapsulate complex lifecycles and leave UI components small, clean, and declarative.
